page.description: Assign a shift or day off per person per day. Drafts are also used by punching (late/early) and shift-based payroll; "Publish" only controls whether employees can see them. For days without a schedule, fixed-schedule employees follow the default shift and calendar.
page.legendHint: Amber outline = unpublished draft; hover a cell for details
page.draftHint: Click a cell to set that day's shift or day off. Weekends and calendar holidays are shaded. For shift schedules, rest days, mandatory days off and national holidays are all shifted — put them on the actual day off.

cell.choose: Choose the shift or day-off type for this day

shiftTypes.title: Shift Types
shiftTypes.description: Define each shift's start and end times and break. An end time earlier than the start time means an overnight shift.
shiftTypes.name: Shift name
shiftTypes.crossHint: Break time is not counted as working time, which is used by the working-hours alerts. A shift used by a schedule cannot be deleted; deactivate it instead.
shiftTypes.shortNameHint: Shown in schedule cells, up to 4 characters. If blank, the first character of the name is used.

quickFill.title: Quick Fill Schedule
quickFill.description: Pick employees and a date range to fill the same shift or day-off type in one go (or clear).
quickFill.choose: Choose a shift or day-off type

publish.title: Publish the {{month}} schedule?
publish.body: {{count}} draft cell(s) are not yet published. Once published, employees can see them in their portal. Later edits to published cells are reflected for employees too.

check.title: Schedule check
check.hint: Only fully scheduled spans are checked. This is an aid, not a legal ruling; ask HR or a labor consultant about exceptions such as flexible working hours.

types.cycle_days_off: Too few days off in cycle

detail.rest_interval: Only {{gapHours}} hours since the previous shift, under 11 hours
detail.consecutive_days: {{days}} consecutive work days with no day off
detail.no_regular_off: {{days}} consecutive days without a regular day off
detail.no_rest_day: {{days}} consecutive days without a rest day
detail.weekly_hours: {{hours}} scheduled hours that week, over {{limit}} (will generate overtime)
detail.cycle_days_off: Only {{count}} regular/rest days off in this two-week cycle; at least {{required}} are required
detail.daily_normal_hours: Scheduled {{hours}} hours, over the {{limit}}-hour daily normal hours of the two-week flexible schedule (the excess is overtime)
detail.cycle_hours: {{hours}} scheduled hours in this two-week cycle, over {{limit}} (will generate overtime)

preview.stats: After applying: {{added}} new, {{changed}} changed, {{unchanged}} unchanged cells

quickFill.resolves: It would also resolve {{count}} existing warnings

publish.title: {{count}} schedule warnings remain
publish.body: Please review or adjust the schedule before publishing.
publish.confirm: I have reviewed these warnings (e.g. flexible hours approved or consent obtained) and still want to publish

check.cycleHint: Two-week flexible employees: at least one regular day off every seven days, and at least 4 regular/rest days off in each two-week cycle. Cycles repeat every 14 days from the start date set on the employee (the thick line on the left of a cell marks a cycle start).

pattern.description: Pre-schedule everyone selected from a rotation pattern: define a cycle (e.g. 5 work days, a rest day, a regular day off) and it repeats across the range from the start date; with many people you can stagger them in groups. Results are drafts you can adjust cell by cell afterwards.
pattern.anchorHint: Day 1 of the pattern falls on this date. For a 7-day pattern "Mon–Fri work, Sat rest day, Sun regular day off", choose a Monday.
pattern.weekPreset: Use weekly pattern (5 work days + rest day + regular day off)
pattern.brush: Brush (pick one, then click the cells below)
pattern.hint: Cells marked "Leave as is" keep the existing schedule. Weekdays below the cells follow the start date.
pattern.groupHint: E.g. groups of 2, shifted 1 day each: people 1–2 start at pattern day 1, people 3–4 at day 2, and so on; 0 = everyone in sync. People are grouped in the order of the list above.
pattern.skipExisting: Do not overwrite cells already scheduled (fill empty cells only)

excel.title: Import/export schedule with Excel
excel.description: One row per employee, one column per day; cells hold a shift code or rest/regular/national day-off codes. The downloaded file includes the current schedule, so you can edit and re-import it.
excel.downloadHint: Downloads the department currently selected. The "說明" sheet lists valid codes; blank = no change, "清除" = delete that cell.
excel.noCells: Nothing to apply (blank cells leave the schedule unchanged).
excel.errors: {{count}} problems; those cells or rows will be skipped
excel.done: Imported {{count}} cells as drafts; publish after reviewing
excel.blankHint: In duty rosters, blank weekdays mean a normal working day. Pick a shift to fill them so schedule checks apply. Codes such as [D] need a shift type with the same short name in Shift Types.
